summary: Confirmed DONE (65af92766 and 60633eff3). Direct clients no longer open /ws/device or request a second ws-token on connect. Device RPCs and the event stream use the main /ws socket, and the dedicated socket opens only for screenshots, as a fallback for older servers, or closes after 60 s idle. Nothing lists devices on connect or reconnect. The event stream binds only while a thread view or the simulator pane retains the environment. reconnect() no longer awaits a device probe. On the server, the iOS probes are cached and share in-flight promises: xcode-select for 60 s, xcodebuild -version for 5 min keyed on the developer dir, and one simctl list reused for 2 s. Mobile builds no device client at all. Only minor issues remain, and only while the pane is open.

evidence.note: The primary direct client uses createDirectDeviceRpcTransport. DeviceWsTransport is built only inside the openDedicated callback.
The saved environment is the same: the dedicated socket is lazy, so no ws-token POST happens at connect.
Hosted reuses the main HostedWsTransport (manageTransport:false). This was already true before.
request and subscribe go to main. requestBulk (screenshots) and the 'unsupported' fallback acquire the dedicated socket, which closes after DEDICATED_DEVICE_SOCKET_IDLE_MS=60s (line 132).
A non-retryable 'unknown tag' subscription error calls onError('unsupported') and stops, so an old server causes no retry loop on main.
Main /ws merges makeDeviceWsRpcLayer into WsHostedRpcGroup. /ws/device is kept for old clients.
registerDeviceConnection only registers the client and starts nothing.
reconnect is client.reconnect, then refreshMetadata, then bootstrapGate. No inventory read. The old version awaited deviceBinding.refreshInventory (f1be4abc7 connection.ts:317-329).
bindDeviceConnection subscribes only, with no list. Binding is retained by ensureDeviceRuntime and unbinds 60 s after the last release.

Callers are ChatThreadRouteView.tsx:128, DraftChatThreadRouteView.tsx:95 and SimulatorPanel.tsx:166. Thread views retain only the event stream, which is cheap: deviceRpc.ts:122-135 is a plain manager.onEvent.
list and getThreadState run only while the pane is mounted (ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:1536 renders it only when activeMode==='simulator'), on a generation change, or on the 5 s setup poll.

The listing, xcode-select and xcodebuild -version caches store the pending promise, so concurrent list and getThreadState share one simctl. A failed or non-Xcode answer is not kept. Boot passes fresh:true and shutdown clears deviceListing (line 537).
Tests cover one simctl and one xcode-select per list, toolchain reuse across reads, re-reading an unaccepted license or a CLT path, and a fresh listing after boot.
Mobile calls createWsRpcClient without a device client, so mobile has no device cost.

Android availability has a 5 s promise cache. listDevices (emulator -list-avds, adb devices -l, and 2 adb calls per running emulator) has no cache or in-flight dedupe. This matters only when the pane is open.

fixDefects:
No blocking defects; the connect and reconnect cost is gone. Minor items, all verified by reading:
(1) Behaviour change from the lazy stream: an agent's 'device.open-pane-requested' event fires only once per thread and device (DeviceManager.surfaceDeviceForAgent, DeviceManager.ts:963-971, keyed on paneSurfacedUdid). It is now lost if no thread view of that environment was mounted in the last 60 s, for example when the user is on another environment, settings or home. Before, the always-bound stream stored it in pendingOpenByThreadKey until the user opened that thread. Now the pane does not auto-open later. Low impact.
(2) While the pane is open, SimulatorPanel.refresh (SimulatorPanel.tsx:210-214) calls list and getThreadState in parallel, and each runs availability() plus discover() on the server. iOS shares one simctl through the 2 s promise cache. Android listDevices runs twice per refresh (about 2+2N processes each) and repeats every 5 s during setup polling. getThreadState already returns devices and availability, so the list call is redundant.
(3) Cosmetic: the ws.ts:99-101 comment says /ws/device is used only for older servers, but current clients also open it for screenshots (requestBulk).
implementationSketch: Optional cleanup, all low priority. (a) SimulatorPanel.refresh: call only api.getThreadState({threadId}) and derive the inventory from the snapshot via applyThreadSnapshot, which already sets environment devices and availability. Alternatively, add a server-side DeviceManager.snapshot path that reuses one availability/discover result. Update SimulatorPanel.browser.tsx mocks. (b) AndroidEmulatorBackend.listDevices: add the same pattern as IosSimulatorBackend.listDevicesUnchecked, a 2 s pending-promise cache that boot and shutdown drop, plus a unit test like IosSimulatorBackend.probeCache.test.ts that counts adb and emulator spawns per DeviceManager.list. (c) To keep agent pane auto-open without an always-on stream, DeviceManager could keep the last open-pane request per thread in memory for a few minutes and replay it to new subscribers in makeDeviceEventStream (deviceRpc.ts:122-135). This is server-only and backward compatible, because clients already dedupe by consuming per thread. Another option is to expose paneSurfacedUdid in ThreadDeviceState. (d) Fix the ws.ts comment.
decisionReason: Nothing required remains. Replaying open-pane requests (item c) is a small server-side behaviour choice that does not touch auth, E2EE, Hub or hosted lifecycle.
correction: The auditor's DONE is correct. They missed two things: the minor open-pane-request regression caused by the lazy event stream, and that SimulatorPanel's parallel list and getThreadState double the uncached Android discovery while the pane is open. Their 'availability and adb devices are not shared with discovery' note understates this, because Android listDevices itself runs twice per refresh.
